review_notes: The 50% surcharge is applied to the entire aggregate charge after multiplication by `num_services`, so if only one berthing service is late, outside ordinary working hours, or cancelled after standby, every service on the call is surcharged. Section 3.8 applies the surcharge to the qualifying service (“If the service either terminates or commences…”), not automatically to all berthing and unberthing services. Model the 50% addition only for each affected service using conditional per-service surcharge components/separate event facts; if the number of affected services cannot be represented, omit this extra with a note rather than applying it call-wide. A cancelled staffing request also should not surcharge unrelated completed movements merely because they are included in `num_services`.
critic_verdict.research_notes: For Durban, use the Section 3.8 'Other Ports' column because Durban has no dedicated column in this table: basic fee 2,801.91 plus 13.68 per 100 tons or part thereof, per service. Charge scope and service counting are in chunk 490: entering/leaving, berth shifts/warping (including to/from drydock or slipway), engine trials, remooring, crewing, and berthing-gang standby/detention; staff conveyance is included; berthing and unberthing are separate services. Tonnage is gross tonnage under the Tonnage Convention 1969 and is not converted to cubic metres; if the certificate is unavailable, use the highest tonnage in Lloyd's Register. Durban ordinary working hours are 00:01–24:00 (24-hour service), with marine operations on public holidays available by special request. A 50% surcharge applies if the service starts or ends outside ordinary working hours, if an outside-hours staff request is cancelled after standby starts, or if the vessel arrives/departs at least 30 minutes after notified time. General marine terms also state no fee for services performed for the port's convenience. The special hourly tanker-attendance rate in chunk 492 is only for Mossel Bay and Saldanha, so it does not apply at Durban.

notes: The supplied ChargeRule schema permits only predefined engine quantities as band and unit bases. It does not permit tariff_tonnage or drydock_occupancy_hours facts to be used as calculation bases.

The schema also has no mechanism to clamp the first-period component to 48 570.64 and independently clamp every subsequent-period component to 20 389.12. Encoding either minimum as an additional fee would incorrectly add it instead of applying the greater of the calculated fee and the minimum.

Accordingly, the published numeric components are not encoded using gross_tonnage or time_in_port_hours, because those substitutions would produce incorrect charges. Exact pricing requires schema support for numeric-fact calculation bases and separate component-level minimums.

The printed bands are consecutive: 0 to 30 000, 30 001 to 60 000, and 60 001 up to 80 000 tariff tons. A continuous numeric representation would require boundary semantics suitable for tariff tonnage values between the printed integer boundaries.
The 40% overstay penalty is not encoded because it applies to each subsequent 12-hour period of overstay and cannot be limited to those periods by the available adjustment model.

issues: Model the 25% outside-hours/Sunday/public-holiday surcharge per affected service, not as 25% of the entire call total. Section 3.6 says the surcharge is payable “for a service either commencing or terminating outside ordinary working hours ... or on Sundays and public holidays.” As written, if only one of two services occurs on Sunday, the adjustment surcharges both services after the num_services multiplier. Split/evaluate services separately or use a conditional per-service surcharge component.
review_notes: Model the additional-craft surcharges against the fee for the particular service and per additional tug/vessel. The current 50% or 100% adjustment is calculated on the whole base after multiplication by `num_services`, so one additional tug supplied for one movement surcharges every movement. Section 3.6 states “50% is payable per tug when an additional tug/vessel is provided” and similarly makes the 100% surcharge apply to an additional tug/vessel requested for a powerless vessel.

Model a cancelled outside-hours standby as an additional deemed-performed service charged at the normal fee plus 25%, rather than merely adding 25% to all existing performed-service fees. With no performed services the current rule charges zero, and with multiple services it surcharges all of them. Section 3.6 says that after standby commences, “the fees as if the service had been performed, are payable, i.e. normal fees enhanced by 25%.”
critic_verdict.research_notes: Use the dedicated Durban column in section 3.6. Base fee is per service, based on vessel gross tonnage, for assistance/attendance within the port; the port decides craft type and number. Craft allocation by tonnage is: up to 2,000 = 0.50 (a workboat); 2,000–10,000 = 1 craft; 10,001–50,000 = 2; 50,001–100,000 = 3; 100,000+ = 4. Durban rates: up to 2,000 = 8,140.00; 2,001–10,000 = 12,633.99 plus 268.99 per additional 100 tons or part above 2,000; 10,000–50,000 = 38,494.51 plus 84.95 per additional 100 tons or part above 10,000; 50,001–100,000 = 73,118.07 plus 32.24 per additional 100 tons or part above 50,000; above 100,000 = 93,548.13 plus 23.65 per additional 100 tons or part above 100,000. Vessel tonnage means gross tonnage under the Tonnage Convention 1969, not converted to cubic metres; if the certificate is unavailable, use the highest tonnage in Lloyd's Register. Durban ordinary working hours are 00:01–24:00 (24-hour service); marine operations are available by special request on public holidays. Apply section 3.6 adjustments: 25% if service begins or ends outside ordinary working hours on weekdays/Saturdays, or on Sundays/public holidays; 50% per additional tug/vessel beyond the allocation when requested by the master or required for safety by the Harbour Master; 50% for a vessel without own power, or 100% where an additional tug/vessel is requested by the master for such a vessel; cancellation after outside-hours standby starts is charged as performed at normal fee plus 25%; arrival/departure at least 30 minutes late costs 8,050.76 per tug per half-hour or part thereof at Durban (all ports except Saldanha). General exemption: no fee for a service performed for the convenience of the port.
